about: A pool to measure how late the filler's fills land (ops/sim_keeper.py --measure), not to sell: one line of 1 000 for 9 USDC, so 160 locked, and the widest fill window, 60 blocks, so that a late fill is measured and not lapsed. The first pool's window is set from what it measures. Its one code, MEASURE, is the creator's own with no share: every sale names a code.
terms_text: Simulated pool for measuring fills, testnet. Not for sale. Simulated pool, testnet. Both stages are paper exams on nobody's money; prices are testnet USDC. An exam costs the price of its line: 1 000 for 9. Each stage: profit target 10 % of the size, no more than 6 % below the starting balance, no more than 3 % below the day's first snapshot (equity with open profit, taken in the first minutes of the UTC day), leverage at most 10x on BTC and ETH and 5x on SOL, thirty days at most, with no minimum of trading days. A fill takes the book's price, never better than the oracle's and at most 1.5 % worse, and pays 0.045 % of its notional, Hyperliquid's taker fee. Whoever passes the exam starts the stage within seven days; whoever passes the stage is paid 8 % of the size, once: no sooner than 72 hours after the payout is claimed, and then once the pool's approver has approved it, or 7 days after it is claimed without approval. The platform's keeper claims a payout as soon as the stage has passed; a payout that may be paid is paid by a call anyone may make, which the keeper makes in its next pass. Payouts are paid in the order they were claimed, out of the money the pool holds: one still waiting for its approval keeps its place, and a later one is paid past it only if the money also covers every payout so passed over; one the pool cannot cover waits, and every payout after it, until money comes in. The pool's creator may change its approver at any time; whoever approves, no payout waits for approval longer than 7 days after it is claimed. Until it is paid, the platform's checker may stop it with a reason written on chain: opposite positions with another account of the platform, that and wallets linked, or a result disputed (a flaw of the exam, the oracle or the filler). A stopped payout stays in the pool for at least 14 days while the trader can object, unless the checker lifts the stop within them and it is paid as any payout; after them anyone may make the stop final, and only from then is the money the pool's. Every exam is bought with a trading group's code, which the pool's creator sets with the address of the group's owner and the owner's share, none or 40 to 60 %; once a sale names a code, neither changes. When the creator takes money out of the pool, each code's owner is sent its share of the profit taken (what is above the payouts owed, held and kept, and above what the creator put in, less the platform's part) in the part of every price the pool took that its code's sales brought. The platform takes 0.5 % of each price and of each withdrawal, and 1 HYPE to open the pool. The pool runs at least 6 months (184 days) from its opening: before then its creator can neither stop its sales nor take back what it put in, only the profit above it, and only the platform can close it sooner, with the money going where it would anyway. The creator withdraws by a request: the money leaves no sooner than 7 days after it, within 3 days after that, only what the pool can spare then, and never more than was asked; the platform may cancel a withdrawal request; it never moves the money. While the pool is open, a funded trader's payout stays in the pool for as long as the stage runs; the creator takes profit only above it, and above three payouts of the largest size. A share paid to a code's owner is never taken back, even if later payouts take the pool's money below what the creator put in. USDC sent to the pool other than by the creator's addToPot is not counted as put in by the creator: it covers payouts as any money of the pool does, and what of it is profit when the creator takes money out (above the payouts owed, held and kept, and above what the creator put in) is shared with the codes' owners as any profit taken.
